questions.q: Why doesn't a "CVSS 9.8 critical" rating, on its own, mean much to an executive or board member?
options: CVSS scores are randomly generated and have no technical basis
CVSS was designed to help prioritize engineering patch work, not to answer the business question of what happens to the company if it goes wrong
Executives are not permitted to see vulnerability scores
CVSS scores only apply to vulnerabilities found by a specific scanning vendor
questions.explain: CVSS is genuinely useful for technical prioritization, but it was never designed to answer the business question an executive actually has — what this means for revenue, regulatory exposure, or reputation.

questions.q: What are the four stages of the translation chain described in this lesson?
options: Technical finding, threat scenario, business consequence, dollar range
Scan, patch, retest, close ticket
Discovery, triage, assignment, remediation
CVSS score, CVE ID, vendor advisory, patch release date
questions.explain: The chain moves a finding from a technical description, through a realistic attacker scenario, into business-consequence categories executives track, and finally into a quantified dollar range.

questions.q: In FAIR, what does Loss Magnitude (LM) represent, and how is it typically split?
options: The number of systems affected, split by operating system
How much a single loss event costs if it happens, split into primary loss (direct costs) and secondary loss (knock-on costs like fines and reputational damage)
The CVSS exploitability sub-score, split into network and local vectors
How many business units were notified, split by region
questions.explain: Loss Magnitude estimates the cost of a single event as a range, divided into primary loss (incident response, replacement, lost productivity) and secondary loss (fines, legal settlements, reputational and customer-attrition costs).

questions.q: What real weakness with red/yellow/green risk heat maps does this lesson point out, citing critiques such as Tony Cox's work on risk matrices?
options: They are illegal to use in regulated industries
They take longer to produce than a quantitative FAIR analysis
They cannot be printed in color in most office environments
They create a false sense of precision and compress very different risks into the same colored cell, with no sense of actual financial exposure
questions.explain: Heat maps are useful as an at-a-glance summary layer, but using them as the sole basis for a decision hides real differences in exposure that only a quantitative range like FAIR reveals.

questions.q: In the worked checkout-system example, what makes the final translated sentence understandable to a CFO or general counsel without any security background?
options: It restates the CVSS vector string in full
It lists every technical detail of the vulnerability's exploit chain
It frames the scenario in terms of lost revenue, mandatory breach notification, and contractual penalties, rather than CVSS terminology
It omits any mention of dollar amounts to avoid overwhelming the reader
questions.explain: The sentence translates the finding entirely into business-consequence categories — revenue, regulatory, contractual — that a CFO or counsel already tracks, with no need to know what CVSS or RCE mean.
